description: Acquire INCLUDE-50, train the GCN, and evaluate on the OFFICIAL signer-independent INCLUDE-50 test split — the end-to-end accuracy proof. Depends on FEAT-001/002/003 (all code must exist and be green). This feature contains the ONLY user-blocking gate: the measured multi-GB download must be surfaced and approved BEFORE any fetch. Implements design sections 5 (download gate with a MEASURED size), 7.3 (honest signer-independent evaluation protocol + gate floors). Success criterion = signer-INDEPENDENT top-1 AND top-5 on features/test (= test_include50.csv), never a random split, never the user's own clips.
steps: tools/select_include50_downloads.py (NEW): needs only the 47 KB include_metadata.zip (no video). Apply the same byte-exact header assertion; parse train_include50.csv + test_include50.csv; map each referenced Category to its Zenodo whole-category zip set (URLs of the form https://zenodo.org/record/4010759/files/<Category>_<i>of<n>.zip per data/raw/include/download_data.sh); HEAD each zip for Content-Length; print the category list + summed byte total AND the 'wasted' fraction vs the clips actually needed (because Zenodo serves whole-category zips).

SURFACE the measured total to the user via send_message (severity 'warning') and WAIT: present option (A) download the measured INCLUDE-50 category-zip set [recommended] vs (B) full INCLUDE-263 (~56 GB). Do NOT fetch gigabytes until the user approves. If any plan step would change what the user sees or how the system behaves beyond the approved scope, stop and ask.

After approval: download the approved Zenodo category zips, extract, keep only clips present in the two CSVs. Run training/prepare_include.py --split-csv-train <train_include50.csv> --split-csv-test <test_include50.csv> ... to build the two [T,27,2] feature trees + label_map.json.

Optionally run tools/import_openhands_weights.py first (263-class warm-start, fail-closed) and record warmstart_loaded_fraction. Train the DecoupledGCN with training/train.py --arch decoupled_gcn --official-split ... (train-time ShearTransform/RotationTransform augmentation per design 3.2; VAL carved from TRAIN only), then train the ST-GCN second ensemble member the same way.

Run tools/pick_thresholds.py --official-split on a TRAIN-derived VAL slice (never the test tree); run tools/sync_vocabulary.py to regenerate config/vocabulary.json; export both members with training/export_onnx.py (GCN branch) and write models/ensemble.json with feature_kind:'graph'.

EVALUATE: load features/test (= test_include50.csv) EXACTLY ONCE at the end; report top-1 and top-5, plus accepted-accuracy and coverage at the tuned thresholds; assert the leakage guards (train/test trees path-disjoint AND stratified_split not on the official path). Record all gate numbers next to warmstart_loaded_fraction in the run metadata.

Apply the go/no-go gate (ALL must hold to consider INCLUDE-263): official-test top-1 >= 70%; accepted-accuracy >= 85% at tuned thresholds; a manual webcam check showing >= 2 distinct accepted labels (refuting the single-label collapse). If any floor is missed, diagnose the pipeline — do NOT download INCLUDE-263.
Confirm one backend boots on port 8000 (no --reload) and logs the loaded graph ensemble; keep the rest of the app working.
acceptance_criteria: The measured INCLUDE-50 download size (summed Content-Length over the needed category zips) is computed from the 47 KB metadata and surfaced to the user BEFORE any multi-GB download, and no gigabytes are fetched without approval.
Signer-independent top-1 AND top-5 are produced from features/test (= test_include50.csv) ONLY, loaded exactly once; the numbers and the gate pass/fail are recorded in run metadata.
Leakage guards hold: train/test feature trees are path-disjoint and stratified_split is proven not on the official-split code path.

=== tools/select_include50_downloads.py (NEW) ===
`python tools/select_include50_downloads.py [--metadata-zip <path>] [--download-sh data/raw/include/download_data.sh] [--no-head] [--json-out <path>]`. Needs ONLY the 47 KB include_metadata.zip (downloaded on demand or local). Applies the byte-exact snapshot assertion (47041 B) and the same byte-exact CSV header guard ['Category','Word','Video','FilePath'] as prepare_include.py. Parses the <Category>_${i}of<n>.zip URL list out of download_data.sh for the authoritative per-category zip counts (the URLs are shell-templated with ${i}, only Seasons is literal 1of1 — regex handles both). Maps CSV Category (spaces) -> Zenodo zip stem (underscores). PRIMARY size source = Zenodo REST API https://zenodo.org/api/records/4010759 (exact per-file sizes, no video fetch) with retry loop; Zenodo HEAD on the file URLs is unreliable (returns 504 Gateway Time-out) so it is only a fallback. Reports category list + per-category sizes + summed total + 'wasted' clip fraction. Report JSON written to runs/include50_download_measure.json.

=== MEASURED RESULT (the gate number) ===
INCLUDE-50 (train_include50.csv 766 rows + test_include50.csv 192 rows = 958 clips) references ALL 15 categories = ALL 46 Zenodo zips = **52.85 GiB (56,751,819,975 bytes)**. Wasted clip fraction = **77.4%** (clips in those categories not among the 50 words; Zenodo serves whole categories). CRITICAL: the INCLUDE-50 'subset' pulls the ENTIRE Zenodo record (full record total is also 52.85 GiB), so option A (INCLUDE-50) and option B (full INCLUDE-263) are the SAME download. The design's recommended-A-because-smaller premise does not hold for this record; the only saving of A is in the prepare/train stage (keep only the 958 clips in the CSVs). Surfaced to the user via send_message (severity warning); WAITING for approval before downloading.
